subject: oop-in-java
name: OOP in Java
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance). Confirm the split in your college's notice.

units.title: Object-Oriented Concepts and Java Fundamentals
summary: OOP organises programs around objects that combine state and behaviour, with four guiding pillars.
Java compiles to bytecode that the JVM runs; the garbage collector manages memory.
Primitive types are fixed-size and overflow silently; reference types are objects on the heap.
Control statements, arrays and formatted I/O are the foundation for the class design of the next unit.

units.title: Classes, Objects, Constructors and Encapsulation
topics: Eight benefits of good class design

sections.title: Eight benefits of good class design

summary: A class defines the state and behaviour of its objects; constructors create valid objects.
Encapsulation through private fields and validated methods keeps objects consistent.
Static members belong to the class; instance members belong to each object.
References explain aliasing, parameter passing and why equals/hashCode must be overridden for value-like classes.
Enums, records and nested classes express fixed sets, data carriers and helper types.

units.title: Inheritance, Polymorphism, Abstract Classes and Interfaces
topics: The Object class and design guidance
Eight uses of inheritance, polymorphism and interfaces

sections.title: The Object class and design guidance
Eight uses of inheritance, polymorphism and interfaces

summary: Inheritance reuses and specialises; constructors chain upward.
Overridden methods are chosen at run time by the object's class, which is what lets one loop handle many shapes.
Abstract classes share implementation among related types; interfaces define capabilities and enable lambdas.
Good designs favour small interfaces and composition, keeping subclasses substitutable for their parents.

units.title: Exception Handling, Strings and Wrapper Classes
topics: Two pictures: the exception family and the string pool
Eight benefits of exception handling and of immutable strings

sections.title: Two pictures: the exception family and the string pool
Eight benefits of exception handling and of immutable strings

summary: Exceptions separate error handling from normal logic; the compiler enforces handling of checked ones.
try-with-resources and finally guarantee clean-up.
Strings are immutable shared objects; builders make repeated modification efficient.
Wrapper classes bridge primitives and objects, with pitfalls around null and ==.

units.title: Generics, Collections, Lambdas, Streams and File I/O
topics: The framework map and the stream pipeline
Eight uses of collections, lambdas and streams

sections.title: The framework map and the stream pipeline
Eight uses of collections, lambdas and streams

summary: Generics make collections type-safe, and the framework offers the right structure for each access pattern.
Choosing between list, set, map, queue and their implementations is a question of ordering, uniqueness and cost.
Lambdas and streams express filter-map-reduce logic concisely and safely.
File I/O is done with buffered, closed-after-use readers and writers or the Files helpers.

units.title: Multithreading, GUI Event Handling and Database Access
topics: Putting it together: a small project design
Threads, servers and databases in pictures
Eight uses of threads, GUI and JDBC

sections.title: Putting it together: a small project design
Threads, servers and databases in pictures
Eight uses of threads, GUI and JDBC

summary: Threads give concurrency, but shared mutable state needs synchronisation to avoid races and deadlocks.
Executors, atomics and concurrent collections are safer than raw threads and locks.
GUI programs are event driven: components register listeners and long work moves off the UI thread.
JDBC connects Java to SQL databases; prepared statements and transactions make it safe.
A real project combines classes, interfaces, generics, collections, exceptions, I/O, threads and a database.
